          it could only learn by looking, and the multi-draft case could never
          be reported because the tag had already selected one.

          This is not a "newest wins" heuristic: exactly one candidate, or an
          error naming every candidate.
      dry_run:
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
        description: |
          When true, run every validation gate but do not call
          `gh release edit --draft=false`. Per spec §Operational contract SHOULD.
      app-id:
        description: |
          Numeric GitHub App ID of the portfolio App. When set, the
          reusable mints a short-lived installation token from
          `secrets.app-private-key` and uses it for the release-edit and
          gh CLI calls in this workflow. When empty (the default), the
          reusable falls through to `secrets.token` — typically the
          consumer's `GITHUB_TOKEN`. The App-authored release:published
          event cascades to release-cd-refresh-master and release-cd-
          deliver-docs, closing the GITHUB_TOKEN cascade gap (issue #330,
          spec/project/workflow-health/ §Known platform constraints).
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ""
      asset-filename:
        description: |
          Name of the HACS zip-release asset the publish step builds and
          attaches (HACS source only). When set, it takes precedence over
          the implicit `hacs.json .filename` read; when empty (the default),
          the reusable falls back to `hacs.json .filename` and finally to
          `<domain>.zip`. This input only decouples the *build* name from
          hacs.json — it does NOT replace the consumer's hacs.json
          `filename`/`zip_release` keys, which are HACS's own contract (HACS
          reads hacs.json to decide which release asset to download). The two
          MUST agree: a mismatch means HACS looks for an asset the reusable
          never built. See spec/ha/hacs-release §ZIP release distribution.
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ""
      auto-align:
        description: |
          Opt-in to the spec's "Primary path: Workflow-driven"
          (spec/project/release-automation/ §Version-bearing file
          alignment). When true AND an App installation token is
          available (inputs.app-id set + secrets.app-private-key valid),
          the reusable updates every version-bearing file to the target
          tag under its transform, commits `chore(release): <tag>` on
          develop authored by the App, pushes, and realigns the draft's
          target_commitish to the new SHA. When false (the default) — or
          when no App token is present — the reusable only verifies
          alignment and leaves the `chore(release): <tag>` commit to the
          operator fallback path. The opt-in plus the App-token presence
          together enforce the spec's "MUST NOT be enabled until the
          portfolio App/PAT is installed and `.github/settings.yml`
          explicitly names the credential as a bypass actor": no token or
          no opt-in ⇒ no write ⇒ fallback. A push rejected by develop's
          branch protection degrades gracefully — the step warns and the
          Verify step below produces the operator-fallback message rather
          than wedging the release.
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      require-cascade:
        description: |
          Require `release-cd-refresh-master.yml` to exist and be active before
          publishing. On by default, because the failure it prevents is the one
          #414 describes: a green release leaving the presentation branch
          stale, unnoticed for weeks.

          Set false only for a repository that deliberately has no presentation
          branch to refresh. The gate's own error message told the reader to
          "remove this gate deliberately" and gave them no way to do it -- this
          input is that way. Without it, a repository that retires its cascade
          can never publish again (issue #437).

          The gate still refuses when the workflow exists but is disabled, and
          that is not affected by this input: a cascade that is present and
          switched off is a different fact from one that was never wanted.
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: true
      expected-target-sha:
        description: |
          The commit the release archive was built from. Feed it from
          `needs.<archive-job>.outputs.target-sha` of
          `reusable-release-archive.yml`, so the tag lands on the commit the
          archive and its provenance record name (issue #456).

          Empty (the default) keeps today's behaviour exactly. Set, the
          workflow refuses to publish when the draft target is not that
          commit -- checked right after the draft is resolved, and again
          immediately before the flip, which pins the target to the SHA in
          the same edit so a branch-named target cannot move in between.

          It cannot be combined with `auto-align: true`: alignment commits on
          develop and moves the draft target after the archive was built, so
          the two would always disagree. Align first through the
          `chore(release): <tag>` PR, then run archive and publish.
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ""
    secrets:
      token:
        required: true
      app-private-key:
        description: |
          PEM-encoded private key for the App identified by `inputs.app-id`.
          Required when `app-id` is set; ignored otherwise.
        required: false

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: release-publish
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  publish:
    name: Publish Release
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write # flips the release draft to published
    steps:
      # Mint an App installation token only when the caller has set
      # inputs.app-id. The output token (when present) replaces
      # secrets.token everywhere downstream in this job via the
      # steps.app-token.outputs.token || secrets.token fallback.
      - name: Mint App installation token
        id: app-token
        if: ${{ inputs.app-id != '' }}
        # Tolerate a half-configured setup. On any failure outputs.token
        # is empty and the fallback to secrets.token kicks in — release-
        # publish keeps working, the cascade gap returns silently.
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/create-github-app-token@fee1f7d63c2ff003460e3d139729b119787bc349 # v2.2.2
        with:
          app-id: ${{ inputs.app-id }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.app-private-key }}

      - name: Checkout develop
        uses: actions/checkout@d23441a48e516b6c34aea4fa41551a30e30af803 # v6.1.0
        with:
          ref: develop
          fetch-depth: 0
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || secrets.token }}
          # Kept: the "Align version-bearing files (primary path)" step
          # runs `git push origin HEAD:develop` with this credential.
          persist-credentials: true

      - name: Resolve draft
        id: draft
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || secrets.token }}
          REQUESTED_TAG: ${{ inputs.tag }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Masks $1 for a log line (#492): control characters become '?' and
          # '##[' becomes '#?[', so the value can neither end the line nor open
          # the runner's older '##[command]' syntax in the middle of one.
          shown() { local v="${1//[[:cntrl:]]/?}"; printf '%s' "${v//\#\#\[/#?[}"; }
          # gh release list on the runner CLI does not expose targetCommitish;
          # resolve the target via gh release view per matching tag.
          drafts=$(gh release list --json isDraft,tagName --jq '[.[] | select(.isDraft == true)]')
          total=$(echo "$drafts" | jq 'length')

          if [[ "$total" == "0" ]]; then
            echo "::error::No draft release found. Run release-drafter.yml on develop first."
            exit 1
          fi

          if [[ -z "$REQUESTED_TAG" ]]; then
            # Omitted tag: exactly one candidate, or an error naming every one
            # of them. Never "newest wins" -- picking silently is how a release
            # gets published from a draft nobody was looking at.
            if [[ "$total" != "1" ]]; then
              echo "::error::No tag given and $total drafts are open. Pass 'tag' explicitly. Open drafts:"
              # Draft tag names are editable text, listed with control
              # characters masked as in the target messages below (#492).
              echo "$drafts" | jq -r '.[] | "  - \(.tagName | gsub("[[:cntrl:]]"; "?") | gsub("##\\["; "#?["))"' >&2
              exit 1
            fi
            TAG=$(echo "$drafts" | jq -r '.[0].tagName')
          else
            TAG="$REQUESTED_TAG"
          fi

          # The tag is the caller's input or a draft's tag name, and every later
          # step reads it from this step's output. A line end in it could start a
          # workflow command in any message that prints the tag or add an entry
          # to $GITHUB_OUTPUT, and '##[' opens the runner's older command syntax
          # anywhere in a log line (ActionCommand.TryParse in actions/runner,
          # read from source, not measured on a runner). Both are refused here,
          # before the first message that prints the tag and before the output
          # write, so no later '$TAG' carries either (#492). Only this message
          # shows it, masked.
          #
          # Git refuses ASCII control characters, DEL and '[' in a ref name, so
          # the '##[' rule costs no tag git accepts. The control-character rule
          # is deliberately wider in a UTF-8 locale, where [[:cntrl:]] also
          # matches C1 (U+0080-U+009F) and U+2028/U+2029, which git allows; in
          # the C locale it matches neither. Which locale the runner gives this
          # step was not verified. LF and CR -- what the runner's line
          # splitting needs -- match in every locale, as do ESC and DEL. Read
          # from actions/runner, not measured on a runner: step output is split
          # into lines by StreamReader.ReadLine, at LF, CR and CRLF only
          # (ProcessInvoker.cs), and $GITHUB_OUTPUT at LF (FileCommandManager.cs),
          # so neither C1 nor U+2028/U+2029 ends a line there. A tag carrying
          # one is refused all the same, although git would accept it. Locale behaviour
          # measured with (prints "cntrl"; the same with \u2028, nothing under
          # LC_ALL=C):
          #   LC_ALL=C.UTF-8 bash -c 'x=$(printf "a\u0085b"); [[ $x == *[[:cntrl:]]* ]] && echo cntrl'
          if [[ "$TAG" == *[[:cntrl:]]* || "$TAG" == *'##['* ]]; then
            echo "::error::Tag '$(shown "$TAG")' contains a control character or '##[' (shown as '?' and '#?['); refusing to continue."
            exit 1
          fi

          if [[ -z "$REQUESTED_TAG" ]]; then
            echo "::notice::No tag given; resolved the single open draft '$TAG'."
          else
            match_count=$(echo "$drafts" | jq --arg t "$TAG" '[.[] | select(.tagName == $t)] | length')

            if [[ "$match_count" == "0" ]]; then
              echo "::error::No draft release with tag '$TAG'. Open drafts:"
              echo "$drafts" | jq -r '.[] | "  - \(.tagName | gsub("[[:cntrl:]]"; "?") | gsub("##\\["; "#?["))"' >&2
              exit 1
            fi

            if [[ "$match_count" != "1" ]]; then
              echo "::error::Multiple drafts match tag '$TAG' — release state is corrupt; resolve manually."
              exit 1
            fi
          fi

          # Every later step reads this rather than inputs.tag, which is empty
          # on the resolved path.
          echo "tag=$TAG" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

          target=$(gh release view "$TAG" --json targetCommitish --jq .targetCommitish)
          # Every later step treats target_sha as a pinned commit, so every
          # target form resolves to one here: refs/heads/<branch> (what
          # release-drafter sets), a bare branch name or a SHA in any case (what
          # a draft edited by hand can carry). origin/<name> is tried first, so
          # a branch on origin wins over a local branch and over a tag of the
          # same name -- the checkout above creates a local 'develop' that a
          # bare 'develop' would otherwise hit (#484). Only a name origin does
          # not have falls back to the clone's own refs (short SHA, tag); the
          # reachability check below then rejects anything that is not on
          # origin/develop. The flip step resolves the live target the same way.
          resolve_commit() {
            local ref="$1"
            if [[ "$ref" =~ ^[0-9a-fA-F]{40}$ ]]; then
              echo "${ref,,}"
            elif git rev-parse --verify --quiet "origin/${ref#refs/heads/}^{commit}"; then
              :
            else
              git rev-parse --verify --quiet "${ref}^{commit}"
            fi
          }

          # A full SHA passes resolve_commit unchecked; cat-file confirms it
          # names a commit this clone has.
          # The target is editable text. Control characters are masked before
          # it is printed, so it cannot start a workflow command on a new line.
          shown_target=$(shown "$target")
          if ! sha=$(resolve_commit "$target") || ! git cat-file -e "${sha}^{commit}" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::Draft tag '$TAG' target '$shown_target' resolves to no commit on origin. Re-run release-drafter to refresh draft target."
            exit 1
          fi

          if ! git merge-base --is-ancestor "$sha" origin/develop; then
            echo "::error::Draft tag '$TAG' target SHA $sha is not reachable from origin/develop. Re-run release-drafter to refresh draft target."
            exit 1
          fi

          # Class guard: whatever the resolution above becomes, nothing but a
          # full lowercase commit SHA leaves this step as target_sha.
          if [[ ! "$sha" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]]; then
            echo "::error::Draft tag '$TAG' target '$shown_target' resolved to '$(shown "$sha")', not a full 40-character commit SHA. Refusing to continue."
            exit 1
          fi

          echo "target_sha=$sha" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "Draft '$TAG' resolved at $sha (reachable from origin/develop)."

      # Issue #456: the archive is built from the draft target in a separate
      # workflow, and this one resolves the target again. Between the two, a
      # merge on a branch-named target or an edited draft can move it, and the
      # tag would then name a commit the archive was not built from. Runs on
      # the dry run too -- the mismatch is the thing an operator wants to see
      # before committing to a publish. Refuses before any write.
      - name: Check the draft target against the expected commit
        if: ${{ inputs.expected-target-sha != '' }}
        env:
          EXPECTED_TARGET_SHA: ${{ inputs.expected-target-sha }}
          AUTO_ALIGN: ${{ inputs.auto-align }}
          TAG: ${{ steps.draft.outputs.tag }}
          DRAFT_TARGET: ${{ steps.draft.outputs.target_sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Masks $1 for a log line (#492): control characters become '?' and
          # '##[' becomes '#?[', so the value can neither end the line nor open
          # the runner's older '##[command]' syntax in the middle of one.
          shown() { local v="${1//[[:cntrl:]]/?}"; printf '%s' "${v//\#\#\[/#?[}"; }
          # Encode, then wrap, for the step summary (#506): a control character
          # becomes a question mark and an ASCII punctuation character its
          # numeric HTML entity (`@` also gets an empty comment after it, so no
          # e-mail autolink forms), inside <code> (md_code) or <pre> (md_pre,
          # line ends kept). Draft, caller and repository text then renders as
          # text and links nothing.
          md_enc() { local LC_ALL=C; local s="${1//[[:cntrl:]]/?}" c n x; s="${s//$'\xc2'[$'\x80'-$'\x9f']/?}"; s="${s//$'\xe2\x80'[$'\xa8\xa9']/?}"; for n in {33..47} {58..64} {91..96} {123..126}; do printf -v x '%x' "$n"; printf -v c '%b' "\\x$x"; s=${s//"$c"/$'\x01'$n$'\x02'}; done; s=${s//$'\x01'64$'\x02'/$'\x01'64$'\x02\x03'}; s=${s//$'\x01'/'&#'}; s=${s//$'\x02'/';'}; s=${s//$'\x03'/'<!-- -->'}; printf '%s' "$s"; }
          md_code() { printf '<code>%s</code>' "$(md_enc "$1")"; }
          md_pre() { local line; printf '<pre>'; while IFS= read -r line; do md_enc "${line%$'\r'}"; printf '\n'; done <<< "$1"; printf '</pre>\n'; }
          expected="${EXPECTED_TARGET_SHA,,}"
          if [[ ! "$expected" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]]; then
            # Printed exactly when it failed the check, so it is the caller's
            # text as given: control characters masked (#492).
            echo "::error::expected-target-sha '$(shown "$EXPECTED_TARGET_SHA")' is not a full 40-character commit SHA. Pass needs.<archive-job>.outputs.target-sha from reusable-release-archive.yml unchanged."
            exit 1
          fi

          if [[ "$AUTO_ALIGN" == "true" ]]; then
            echo "::error::expected-target-sha cannot be combined with auto-align: true. Alignment commits on develop and moves the draft target after the archive was built, so the tag could never land on the archived commit. Align first through the 'chore(release): $TAG' PR, then run archive and publish with auto-align off."
            exit 1
          fi

          # Resolve draft has already turned every target form into a full
          # lowercase commit SHA read from origin, so this compares commit to
          # commit without resolving again.
          actual="$DRAFT_TARGET"

          if [[ "$actual" != "$expected" ]]; then
            echo "::error::Draft '$TAG' targets $actual, but the archive was built from $expected. Likely a merge landed on the target branch after the archive was built, or the draft target was changed. Nothing was published; rebuild the archive from the current draft target, then publish again."
            exit 1
          fi

          echo "Draft '$TAG' target $actual matches the expected commit."
          { echo; echo "- Draft target $(md_code "$actual") matches the archived commit (expected-target-sha)."; } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      - name: Detect project type and load version-bearing files
        id: vbf
        env:
          TAG: ${{ steps.draft.outputs.tag }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          python3 -c "import yaml" 2>/dev/null || pip install --quiet pyyaml

          python3 - <<'PY' > vbf.json
          import json, pathlib, re, sys

          def shown(value):
              # Paths come from .github/release-automation.yml, repository
              # content. Before a message prints one, control characters become
              # '?' and '##[' becomes '#?[', so neither a line end nor the
              # runner's older '##[command]' syntax can start a command (#492).
              return re.sub(r"[\x00-\x1f\x7f-\x9f]", "?", str(value)).replace("##[", "#?[")

          override_path = pathlib.Path(".github/release-automation.yml")
          if override_path.exists():
              import yaml
              data = yaml.safe_load(override_path.read_text()) or {}
              entries = data.get("version_bearing_files", [])
              for e in entries:
                  e.setdefault("transform", "strip-leading-v")
                  if "format" not in e:
                      p = e.get("path", "")
                      if p.endswith(".toml"):
                          e["format"] = "toml"
                      elif p.endswith(".json"):
                          e["format"] = "json"
                      else:
                          print(f"::error::Cannot infer format for '{shown(p)}'; declare format: json|toml in .github/release-automation.yml", file=sys.stderr)
                          sys.exit(1)
              json.dump({"source": "override", "entries": entries}, sys.stdout)
              sys.exit(0)

          if pathlib.Path(".claude-plugin/plugin.json").exists():
              entries = [{"path": ".claude-plugin/plugin.json", "selector": "version", "transform": "strip-leading-v", "format": "json"}]
              mp = pathlib.Path(".claude-plugin/marketplace.json")
              if mp.exists():
                  entries.append({"path": ".claude-plugin/marketplace.json", "selector": "metadata.version", "transform": "strip-leading-v", "format": "json"})
                  # Per spec/project/release-automation/ §Version-bearing files the
                  # marketplace.json selector is `$.metadata.version` AND `$.plugins[].version`.
                  # Guard on existence: only emit the array selector when EVERY plugins[]
                  # entry actually declares a version key, so single-plugin repos and repos
                  # whose plugins[] omit version (the claude-shared workaround) don't start
                  # failing verification on a key the wildcard read would not find.
                  try:
                      plugins = (json.loads(mp.read_text()) or {}).get("plugins", [])
                  except (ValueError, OSError):
                      plugins = []
                  if isinstance(plugins, list) and plugins and all(isinstance(p, dict) and "version" in p for p in plugins):
                      entries.append({"path": ".claude-plugin/marketplace.json", "selector": "plugins[].version", "transform": "strip-leading-v", "format": "json"})
              json.dump({"source": "claude-plugin", "entries": entries}, sys.stdout)
              sys.exit(0)

          if pathlib.Path("pyproject.toml").exists():
              import tomllib
              data = tomllib.loads(pathlib.Path("pyproject.toml").read_text())
              if data.get("project", {}).get("version") is not None:
                  json.dump({"source": "python", "entries": [
                      {"path": "pyproject.toml", "selector": "project.version", "transform": "strip-leading-v", "format": "toml"},
                  ]}, sys.stdout)
                  sys.exit(0)

          if pathlib.Path("package.json").exists():
              json.dump({"source": "node", "entries": [
                  {"path": "package.json", "selector": "version", "transform": "strip-leading-v", "format": "json"},
              ]}, sys.stdout)
              sys.exit(0)

          cc = pathlib.Path("custom_components")
          if cc.is_dir():
              manifests = sorted(cc.glob("*/manifest.json"))
              if manifests:
                  json.dump({"source": "hacs", "entries": [
                      {"path": str(p), "selector": "version", "transform": "strip-leading-v", "format": "json"} for p in manifests
                  ]}, sys.stdout)
                  sys.exit(0)

          json.dump({"source": "none", "entries": []}, sys.stdout)
          PY

          source=$(jq -r '.source' vbf.json)
          count=$(jq '.entries | length' vbf.json)
          echo "source=$source" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "count=$count" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "Detected project type: $source ($count version-bearing file(s))"
          # vbf.json holds paths, selectors and, on the override path, whole
          # entries -- keys included -- from the repository. JSON escapes control
          # characters already; '##[' is neutralised in every key and string
          # value as in shown() (#492).
          jq 'walk(if type == "object" then with_entries(.key |= gsub("##\\["; "#?["))
                   elif type == "string" then gsub("##\\["; "#?[") else . end)' vbf.json

      # Shared version-bearing selector grammar, written once and imported by
      # BOTH the align (write) and verify (read) steps so the dot-path + array-
      # wildcard grammar can never drift between them. Grammar: dot-separated
      # parts; a part may carry a trailing `[]` or `[*]` meaning "every element
      # of this array" (spec/project/release-automation/ §Version-bearing files
      # lists `$.plugins[].version`). refs(data, selector) returns (container,
      # key) leaf refs — read via container[key], written via container[key]=v.
      - name: Prepare selector helper
        if: steps.vbf.outputs.count != '0'
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > selectorlib.py <<'PY'
          def refs(data, selector):
              """Return [(container, key), ...] scalar-leaf refs for a dot-path
              selector with optional `[]`/`[*]` array wildcards. Raises
              KeyError/TypeError/IndexError on a path that does not resolve."""
              parts = [p for p in selector.split(".") if p]
              nodes = [data]
              for i, raw in enumerate(parts):
                  if raw.endswith("[]"):
                      key, wild = raw[:-2], True
                  elif raw.endswith("[*]"):
                      key, wild = raw[:-3], True
                  else:
                      key, wild = raw, False
                  last = i == len(parts) - 1
                  nxt = []
                  for n in nodes:
                      child = n[key]
                      if wild:
                          if not isinstance(child, list):
                              raise TypeError(f"selector part '{raw}' is not an array")
                          if last:
                              nxt.extend((child, idx) for idx in range(len(child)))
                          else:
                              nxt.extend(child)
                      else:
                          nxt.append((n, key) if last else child)
                  nodes = nxt
              return nodes
          PY

      # Primary path (spec/project/release-automation/ §Version-bearing file
      # alignment → "Primary path: Workflow-driven"). Runs only when the caller
      # opts in (inputs.auto-align) AND a bypass App token is available
      # (steps.app-token.outputs.token != ''): the workflow then aligns every
      # version-bearing file to the target tag, commits `chore(release): <tag>`
      # on develop authored by the App, and pushes — automating the last manual
      # link end-to-end. The opt-in plus the App-token presence together enforce
      # the spec's enablement gate ("MUST NOT be enabled until the App is
      # installed and named as a bypass actor"): no opt-in or no token ⇒ this
      # step is skipped and the Verify step's operator-fallback message governs
      # (the fallback path stays byte-for-byte unchanged).
      - name: Align version-bearing files (primary path)
        id: align
        if: ${{ inputs.auto-align && steps.app-token.outputs.token != '' && steps.vbf.outputs.count != '0' }}
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || secrets.token }}
          TAG: ${{ steps.draft.outputs.tag }}
          DRY_RUN: ${{ inputs.dry_run }}
          APP_SLUG: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.app-slug }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Encode, then wrap, for the step summary (#506): a control character
          # becomes a question mark and an ASCII punctuation character its
          # numeric HTML entity (`@` also gets an empty comment after it, so no
          # e-mail autolink forms), inside <code> (md_code) or <pre> (md_pre,
          # line ends kept). Draft, caller and repository text then renders as
          # text and links nothing.
          md_enc() { local LC_ALL=C; local s="${1//[[:cntrl:]]/?}" c n x; s="${s//$'\xc2'[$'\x80'-$'\x9f']/?}"; s="${s//$'\xe2\x80'[$'\xa8\xa9']/?}"; for n in {33..47} {58..64} {91..96} {123..126}; do printf -v x '%x' "$n"; printf -v c '%b' "\\x$x"; s=${s//"$c"/$'\x01'$n$'\x02'}; done; s=${s//$'\x01'64$'\x02'/$'\x01'64$'\x02\x03'}; s=${s//$'\x01'/'&#'}; s=${s//$'\x02'/';'}; s=${s//$'\x03'/'<!-- -->'}; printf '%s' "$s"; }
          md_code() { printf '<code>%s</code>' "$(md_enc "$1")"; }
          md_pre() { local line; printf '<pre>'; while IFS= read -r line; do md_enc "${line%$'\r'}"; printf '\n'; done <<< "$1"; printf '</pre>\n'; }
          # Edit every version-bearing file in the checked-out develop tree to the
          # target tag, honouring each file's existing v-prefix convention and
          # every selector match (incl. array wildcards). Format-preserving:
          # JSON via an indent-detecting round-trip, TOML via a targeted regex on
          # the version line — minimal diffs, no whole-file reformat, no tomlkit.
          python3 - <<'PY'
          import json, os, re, sys
          from selectorlib import refs

          tag = os.environ["TAG"]

          with open("vbf.json") as f:
              vbf = json.load(f)

          def shown(value):
              # Paths, selector keys and formats are repository content; masked
              # before a message prints them, as in the detect step (#492).
              return re.sub(r"[\x00-\x1f\x7f-\x9f]", "?", str(value)).replace("##[", "#?[")

          def target_value(existing, tag):
              # strip-leading-v: keep the file's existing convention — write the
              # v-prefixed tag only when the current value already uses a v
              # (spec SHOULD: the workflow MUST NOT silently rewrite the convention).
              return tag if str(existing).startswith("v") else tag.lstrip("v")

          for e in vbf["entries"]:
              path, selector, fmt = e["path"], e["selector"], e["format"]
              raw = open(path).read()
              if fmt == "json":
                  data = json.loads(raw)
                  targets = refs(data, selector)
                  if not targets:
                      continue
                  for c, k in targets:
                      c[k] = target_value(c[k], tag)
                  # Preserve the file's exact indent unit (spaces or tabs):
                  # json.dumps accepts a string indent and uses it verbatim, so a
                  # tab-indented manifest stays tab-indented instead of silently
                  # collapsing to 2 spaces. Default to 2 spaces when undetectable.
                  m = re.search(r"\n([ \t]+)\S", raw)
                  indent = m.group(1) if m else 2
                  open(path, "w").write(json.dumps(data, indent=indent, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
              elif fmt == "toml":
                  # tomllib is read-only; rewrite the single `<key> = "<value>"`
                  # line in place with a targeted regex (no tomlkit dependency).
                  import tomllib
                  data = tomllib.loads(raw)
                  for c, k in refs(data, selector):
                      existing = str(c[k])
                      newval = target_value(existing, tag)
                      pat = re.compile(r'^(\s*' + re.escape(k) + r'\s*=\s*)"' + re.escape(existing) + r'"', re.M)
                      raw, n = pat.subn(lambda mo: mo.group(1) + '"' + newval + '"', raw, count=1)
                      if n == 0:
                          print(f"::error::Could not rewrite {shown(k)} in {shown(path)} (format-preserving regex matched nothing).", file=sys.stderr)
                          sys.exit(1)
                  open(path, "w").write(raw)
              else:
                  print(f"::error::Unsupported format '{shown(fmt)}' for {shown(path)}", file=sys.stderr)
                  sys.exit(1)
          PY

          mapfile -t paths < <(jq -r '.entries[].path' vbf.json | sort -u)

          if git diff --quiet -- "${paths[@]}"; then
            # Already aligned at develop HEAD (a prior primary run or a merged
            # fallback `chore(release)` PR). No commit needed; the draft target is
            # realigned to develop HEAD below so Verify reads the aligned tree.
            committed=false
            new_sha=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
            echo "Version-bearing files already aligned at $new_sha; no commit needed."
          else
            committed=true
            slug="${APP_SLUG:-github-actions}"
            uid=$(gh api "/users/${slug}[bot]" --jq .id 2>/dev/null || echo "")
            git config user.name "${slug}[bot]"
            if [[ -n "$uid" ]]; then
              git config user.email "${uid}+${slug}[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
            else
              git config user.email "${slug}[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
            fi
            git add -- "${paths[@]}"
            git commit -m "chore(release): $TAG"
            new_sha=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
            echo "Committed chore(release): $TAG at $new_sha."
          fi

          if [[ "$DRY_RUN" == "true" ]]; then
            # Dry run: expose the locally-built commit so the Verify step can read
            # the aligned tree via `git show`, but never push or realign the draft.
            echo "target_sha=$new_sha" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::Dry run — aligned locally at ${new_sha:0:8}; not pushing to develop or realigning the draft."
            subject="chore(release): $TAG"
            short_sha="${new_sha:0:8}"
            { echo; echo "### Alignment (dry run)"; echo; echo "- Would commit/push $(md_code "$subject") and realign the draft to $(md_code "$short_sha")."; } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            exit 0
          fi

          # Push the alignment commit (if any). The push authority is the App being
          # a declared bypass actor on develop (branch-protection config, not a
          # workflow `permissions:` key); per spec the push respects
          # `enforce_admins: true` — the bypass is declared, not stolen.
          #
          # A rejected push (e.g. develop's branch protection refuses a direct push
          # because the App is not a permitted bypass actor) MUST NOT wedge the
          # release. Degrade to the operator fallback path: warn, emit no
          # target_sha, and skip the draft realign so the Verify step below falls
          # back to steps.draft.outputs.target_sha — the unaligned draft tree — and
          # surfaces the operator-fallback message
          # (spec/project/release-automation/ §Fallback path).
          if [[ "$committed" == "true" ]]; then
            if ! git push origin HEAD:develop; then
              msg="Primary-path push of 'chore(release): $TAG' to develop was rejected (the App may not be a permitted bypass actor for direct pushes to develop). Falling back to the operator path: open a 'chore(release): $TAG' PR aligning every version-bearing file (spec/project/release-automation/ §Fallback path), then re-run release-publish."
              echo "::warning::$msg"
              # The log line above prints msg unmasked: its only value is TAG,
              # which Resolve draft refused for a control character or '##['
              # (#492). Neither touches Markdown, so the summary writes the same
              # text with the tag encoded (#506).
              subject="chore(release): $TAG"
              {
                echo
                echo "### ⚠️ Alignment push rejected (operator fallback)"
                echo
                echo "Primary-path push of $(md_code "$subject") to develop was rejected (the App may not be a permitted bypass actor for direct pushes to develop). Falling back to the operator path: open a $(md_code "$subject") PR aligning every version-bearing file (spec/project/release-automation/ §Fallback path), then re-run release-publish."
              } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
              exit 0
            fi
            echo "::notice::Pushed alignment commit to develop."
          fi

          # Push succeeded, or no commit was needed because the tree was already
          # aligned at develop HEAD — in both cases new_sha is reachable on develop.
          # Expose it and realign the draft target to that exact SHA so the
          # published tag is cut from this commit.
          echo "target_sha=$new_sha" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          gh release edit "$TAG" --target "$new_sha"
          echo "::notice::Realigned draft '$TAG' target to ${new_sha:0:8}."
          short_sha="${new_sha:0:8}"
          { echo; echo "### Alignment"; echo; echo "- Aligned version-bearing files and set draft $(md_code "$TAG") target to $(md_code "$short_sha")."; } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      - name: Verify version-bearing-file alignment
        if: steps.vbf.outputs.count != '0'
        env:
          TAG: ${{ steps.draft.outputs.tag }}
          TARGET_SHA: ${{ steps.align.outputs.target_sha || steps.draft.outputs.target_sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          python3 - <<'PY'
          import json, os, re, subprocess, sys
          from selectorlib import refs

          tag = os.environ["TAG"]
          sha = os.environ["TARGET_SHA"]

          with open("vbf.json") as f:
              vbf = json.load(f)

          def shown(value):
              # Paths, selectors, file values and commit subjects are
              # repository content; masked before a message prints them, as in
              # the detect step (#492).
              return re.sub(r"[\x00-\x1f\x7f-\x9f]", "?", str(value)).replace("##[", "#?[")

          def data_at_sha(path, sha, fmt):
              raw = subprocess.run(
                  ["git", "show", f"{sha}:{path}"],
                  capture_output=True, text=True, check=True,
              ).stdout
              if fmt == "json":
                  return json.loads(raw)
              elif fmt == "toml":
                  import tomllib
                  return tomllib.loads(raw)
              raise SystemExit(f"::error::Unsupported format '{shown(fmt)}' for {shown(path)}")

          def aligned(actual, tag):
              # transform=strip-leading-v: accept either form, matching the file's existing convention
              return actual == tag or actual == tag.lstrip("v")

          errors = []
          for e in vbf["entries"]:
              try:
                  data = data_at_sha(e["path"], sha, e["format"])
                  # Every selector match (incl. array wildcards) MUST equal the tag.
                  values = [str(c[k]) for c, k in refs(data, e["selector"])]
              except subprocess.CalledProcessError:
                  errors.append(f"{e['path']}: file missing at {sha[:8]}")
                  continue
              except (KeyError, TypeError, IndexError) as exc:
                  errors.append(f"{e['path']}: selector '{e['selector']}' not found ({exc})")
                  continue
              for actual in values:
                  if not aligned(actual, tag):
                      errors.append(f"{e['path']}: {e['selector']} is '{actual}', expected '{tag}' (or '{tag.lstrip('v')}')")

          if errors:
              print("::error::Version-bearing files not aligned to target tag:")
              for line in errors:
                  # The list marker is a literal, so no line starts with
                  # repository text: a leading '::' survives shown() (#492).
                  print(f"  - {shown(line)}")
              print(f"::error::Open a 'chore(release): {tag}' PR aligning every file, or wait for the workflow-driven primary path (when the portfolio App/PAT lands).")
              sys.exit(1)

          print(f"All {len(vbf['entries'])} version-bearing file(s) aligned to {tag}.")

          paths = [e["path"] for e in vbf["entries"]]
          log_args = ["git", "log", "-1", "--pretty=%s", sha, "--"] + paths
          subject = subprocess.run(log_args, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout.strip()

          expected_prefix = f"chore(release): {tag}"
          if not subject.startswith(expected_prefix):
              print(f"::error::No 'chore(release): {tag}' alignment commit at {sha[:8]} touching the version-bearing files.")
              print(f"::error::Most recent commit subject on these paths: '{shown(subject)}'")
              print(f"::error::Per spec/project/release-automation/ §Pre-publish verification, the alignment commit subject must start with '{expected_prefix}'.")
              sys.exit(1)

          print(f"Alignment commit confirmed: '{shown(subject)}'")
          PY

      - name: Disclose target state in job summary
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || secrets.token }}
          TAG: ${{ steps.draft.outputs.tag }}
          TARGET_SHA: ${{ steps.align.outputs.target_sha || steps.draft.outputs.target_sha }}
          DRY_RUN: ${{ inputs.dry_run }}
          VBF_SOURCE: ${{ steps.vbf.outputs.source }}
          VBF_COUNT: ${{ steps.vbf.outputs.count }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Encode, then wrap, for the step summary (#506): a control character
          # becomes a question mark and an ASCII punctuation character its
          # numeric HTML entity (`@` also gets an empty comment after it, so no
          # e-mail autolink forms), inside <code> (md_code) or <pre> (md_pre,
          # line ends kept). Draft, caller and repository text then renders as
          # text and links nothing.
          md_enc() { local LC_ALL=C; local s="${1//[[:cntrl:]]/?}" c n x; s="${s//$'\xc2'[$'\x80'-$'\x9f']/?}"; s="${s//$'\xe2\x80'[$'\xa8\xa9']/?}"; for n in {33..47} {58..64} {91..96} {123..126}; do printf -v x '%x' "$n"; printf -v c '%b' "\\x$x"; s=${s//"$c"/$'\x01'$n$'\x02'}; done; s=${s//$'\x01'64$'\x02'/$'\x01'64$'\x02\x03'}; s=${s//$'\x01'/'&#'}; s=${s//$'\x02'/';'}; s=${s//$'\x03'/'<!-- -->'}; printf '%s' "$s"; }
          md_code() { printf '<code>%s</code>' "$(md_enc "$1")"; }
          md_pre() { local line; printf '<pre>'; while IFS= read -r line; do md_enc "${line%$'\r'}"; printf '\n'; done <<< "$1"; printf '</pre>\n'; }
          created_at=$(gh release view "$TAG" --json createdAt --jq .createdAt)
          # The release title, which the operational contract requires the
          # summary to disclose. A draft's title and its tag are set
          # independently, so a wrong title is invisible when only the tag is
          # shown -- and the title is what readers of the release see first.
          title=$(gh release view "$TAG" --json name --jq .name)
          # The first 800 characters, cut by jq: `head -c` counts bytes and
          # can split a multi-byte character.
          body_head=$(gh release view "$TAG" --json body --jq '(.body // "")[0:800]')
          title_cell="_(empty)_"
          if [[ -n "$title" ]]; then
            title_cell=$(md_code "$title")
          fi

          {
            echo "## Release publish: $(md_code "$TAG")"
            echo
            echo "| Field | Value |"
            echo "|---|---|"
            echo "| Tag | $(md_code "$TAG") |"
            echo "| Title | $title_cell |"
            echo "| Target SHA | $(md_code "$TARGET_SHA") |"
            echo "| Draft created | $(md_code "$created_at") |"
            echo "| Triggerer | @${GITHUB_TRIGGERING_ACTOR:-$GITHUB_ACTOR} |"
            echo "| Run URL | $GITHUB_SERVER_URL/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs/$GITHUB_RUN_ID |"
            echo "| Project type | $(md_code "$VBF_SOURCE") ($(md_code "$VBF_COUNT") file(s)) |"
            echo "| Dry run | $(md_code "$DRY_RUN") |"
            echo
            echo "### Body preview"
            echo
            md_pre "$body_head"
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      # HACS zip-release asset (spec/ha/hacs-release §ZIP release distribution).
      # When the project is a HACS integration, attach a <domain>.zip asset built
      # from the integration directory at the draft's target SHA BEFORE the
      # draft=false flip below — a downstream `on: release published` job would
      # race the user's first download. Gated on the same `hacs` source the
      # version-bearing-file detection already established; a no-op for every
      # other project type.
      #
      # ZIP layout: the contents of custom_components/<domain>/ at the ZIP root
      # (the established integration_blueprint pattern — HACS extracts the named
      # asset into custom_components/<domain>/). content_in_root layouts and
      # non-integration HACS categories are out of scope for this step.
      - name: Attach HACS zip-release asset
        if: steps.vbf.outputs.source == 'hacs'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || secrets.token }}
          TAG: ${{ steps.draft.outputs.tag }}
          TARGET_SHA: ${{ steps.align.outputs.target_sha || steps.draft.outputs.target_sha }}
          DRY_RUN: ${{ inputs.dry_run }}
          ASSET_FILENAME: ${{ inputs.asset-filename }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Masks $1 for a log line (#492): control characters become '?' and
          # '##[' becomes '#?[', so the value can neither end the line nor open
          # the runner's older '##[command]' syntax in the middle of one.
          shown() { local v="${1//[[:cntrl:]]/?}"; printf '%s' "${v//\#\#\[/#?[}"; }
          # Encode, then wrap, for the step summary (#506): a control character
          # becomes a question mark and an ASCII punctuation character its
          # numeric HTML entity (`@` also gets an empty comment after it, so no
          # e-mail autolink forms), inside <code> (md_code) or <pre> (md_pre,
          # line ends kept). Draft, caller and repository text then renders as
          # text and links nothing.
          md_enc() { local LC_ALL=C; local s="${1//[[:cntrl:]]/?}" c n x; s="${s//$'\xc2'[$'\x80'-$'\x9f']/?}"; s="${s//$'\xe2\x80'[$'\xa8\xa9']/?}"; for n in {33..47} {58..64} {91..96} {123..126}; do printf -v x '%x' "$n"; printf -v c '%b' "\\x$x"; s=${s//"$c"/$'\x01'$n$'\x02'}; done; s=${s//$'\x01'64$'\x02'/$'\x01'64$'\x02\x03'}; s=${s//$'\x01'/'&#'}; s=${s//$'\x02'/';'}; s=${s//$'\x03'/'<!-- -->'}; printf '%s' "$s"; }
          md_code() { printf '<code>%s</code>' "$(md_enc "$1")"; }
          md_pre() { local line; printf '<pre>'; while IFS= read -r line; do md_enc "${line%$'\r'}"; printf '\n'; done <<< "$1"; printf '</pre>\n'; }

          # Domain from the first detected manifest path: custom_components/<domain>/manifest.json
          domain=$(jq -r '.entries[0].path' vbf.json \
            | sed -E 's#^custom_components/([^/]+)/manifest\.json$#\1#')
          if [[ -z "$domain" || "$domain" == "null" ]]; then
            echo "::error::Could not derive integration domain from vbf.json entries."
            exit 1
          fi
          # The domain is a directory name, the file name an input or
          # hacs.json content: text the caller or the repository controls.
          # Messages print these masked copies, so a control character can't
          # start a workflow command on a new line (#492). The build itself
          # uses the values unchanged.
          shown_domain=$(shown "$domain")

          # Asset filename resolution (precedence per spec/ha/hacs-release
          # §ZIP release distribution): explicit inputs.asset-filename wins;
          # else hacs.json .filename at the target SHA; else <domain>.zip.
          hacs_filename=""
          if git cat-file -e "$TARGET_SHA:hacs.json" 2>/dev/null; then
            hacs_filename=$(git show "$TARGET_SHA:hacs.json" | jq -r '.filename // empty')
          else
            echo "::warning::No hacs.json at $TARGET_SHA — a HACS integration MUST ship one (spec/ha/hacs-release)."
          fi
          [[ "$hacs_filename" == "null" ]] && hacs_filename=""
          shown_hacs_filename=$(shown "$hacs_filename")

          if [[ -n "$ASSET_FILENAME" ]]; then
            filename="$ASSET_FILENAME"
            # The build name and HACS's own hacs.json contract MUST agree, or
            # HACS downloads an asset this run never built. Warn on divergence.
            if [[ -n "$hacs_filename" && "$hacs_filename" != "$filename" ]]; then
              echo "::warning::asset-filename '$(shown "$filename")' disagrees with hacs.json filename '$shown_hacs_filename' — HACS reads hacs.json to pick the asset, so the two MUST match (spec/ha/hacs-release §ZIP release distribution)."
            fi
          else
            filename="$hacs_filename"
          fi
          [[ -z "$filename" ]] && filename="${domain}.zip"
          shown_filename=$(shown "$filename")
          echo "Building HACS asset '$shown_filename' from custom_components/$shown_domain at ${TARGET_SHA:0:8}."

          # Extract the integration directory from the target tree (independent of
          # the checked-out develop HEAD), then zip its CONTENTS at the root.
          workdir=$(mktemp -d)
          if ! git archive "$TARGET_SHA" "custom_components/$domain" | tar -x -C "$workdir"; then
            echo "::error::custom_components/$shown_domain not found at $TARGET_SHA."
            exit 1
          fi
          srcdir="$workdir/custom_components/$domain"

          # Best-effort determinism: stamp mtimes to the target commit date, sort entries.
          commit_date=$(git show -s --format=%cI "$TARGET_SHA")
          find "$srcdir" -exec touch -d "$commit_date" {} +

          out="$PWD/$filename"
          ( cd "$srcdir" && find . -type f -printf '%P\n' | sort | zip -X -q "$out" -@ )
          # du prints the path after the size; a line break in the file name
          # would put the raw rest of it on a line of its own, so only the
          # first line's size field is kept (#492).
          echo "Built $(du -h "$out" | head -n 1 | cut -f1) asset: $shown_filename"

          if [[ "$DRY_RUN" == "true" ]]; then
            echo "::notice::Dry run — built '$shown_filename' but not uploading to draft '$TAG'."
            { echo; echo "### HACS asset"; echo; echo "- Built $(md_code "$filename") (dry run, not uploaded)."; } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            exit 0
          fi

          # Attach to the still-draft release so the asset is present the instant
          # the next step flips draft=false. --clobber makes re-runs idempotent.
          gh release upload "$TAG" "$out" --clobber
          echo "::notice::Attached '$shown_filename' to draft '$TAG'."
          { echo; echo "### HACS asset"; echo; echo "- Attached $(md_code "$filename") to the release before publish."; } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      # Pre-publish, deliberately. The cascade check below this runs *after* the
      # flip, so it can only report a gap that already happened -- and a release
      # is not revocable. A presentation branch left stale behind a green
      # release is exactly the state #414 describes, and v2.0.0 and v2.0.1 both
      # reached it. Checking first turns "discovered afterwards" into "refused
      # beforehand".
      #
      # `state` distinguishes the two failure modes the spec names: 404 means
      # the workflow is absent, `disabled_inactivity` means GitHub suspended it
      # after 60 days without a scheduled run, and `disabled_manually` means
      # somebody turned it off. All three leave the cascade dead while the
      # release looks healthy.
      - name: Verify the cascade workflow exists and is active
        if: ${{ inputs.dry_run != true && inputs.require-cascade }}
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || secrets.token }}
          CASCADE: release-cd-refresh-master.yml
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Masks $1 for a log line (#492): control characters become '?' and
          # '##[' becomes '#?[', so the value can neither end the line nor open
          # the runner's older '##[command]' syntax in the middle of one.
          shown() { local v="${1//[[:cntrl:]]/?}"; printf '%s' "${v//\#\#\[/#?[}"; }
          if ! state=$(gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/workflows/${CASCADE}" --jq .state 2>/dev/null); then
            echo "::error::${CASCADE} does not exist in this repository. Publishing would leave the presentation branch stale behind a green release (see #414). Add the workflow, or set 'require-cascade: false' if this repository deliberately has no presentation branch."
            exit 1
          fi
          if [[ "$state" != "active" ]]; then
            # An API response; masked like every other printed response (#492).
            echo "::error::${CASCADE} exists but reports state '$(shown "$state")'. GitHub disables a scheduled workflow after 60 days of repository inactivity ('disabled_inactivity'), and it can be switched off by hand ('disabled_manually'). Re-enable it before publishing: gh workflow enable ${CASCADE}"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "Cascade workflow ${CASCADE} is active."

      # This repository, at the commit this workflow runs from, checked out
      # into a directory of its own. Two steps need it: actions/setup-vale and
      # its .vale-version for the Vale check, and scripts/docs_freshness.py for
      # the freshness gate. A `uses: ./...` path resolves in the CALLER's
      # workspace, and a consumer's checkout carries neither, so both come
      # from here -- and at job.workflow_sha they can never be a different
      # version than this file's.
      #
      # Deliberately after the alignment step, which commits on the caller's
      # checkout: the directory is never part of that tree's commit. No
      # continue-on-error: without this checkout the Vale and freshness gates
      # have nothing to run, and a gate that opens when its tool is missing
      # verifies nothing while looking like it does. The job fails here,
      # visibly, before anything is published.
      - name: Check out gh-plumbing at the pinned commit
        uses: actions/checkout@d23441a48e516b6c34aea4fa41551a30e30af803 # v6.1.0
        with:
          repository: ${{ job.workflow_repository }}
          ref: ${{ job.workflow_sha }}
          path: .gh-plumbing
          persist-credentials: false

      # Verified against the committed SHA-256 before it is unpacked (#488).
      # continue-on-error so the next step can apply the failure policy: the
      # action's `result` output tells a download failure from a refusal.
      - name: Install Vale (checksum-verified)
        id: vale
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: ./.gh-plumbing/actions/setup-vale
        with:
          version-file: .gh-plumbing/.vale-version

      # The release notes are the one artefact of a release that nobody reviews
      # again. release-drafter assembles them from pull-request titles and stops
      # touching the release the moment it is published, so the flip freezes the
      # text. This is the last point at which it can still change.
      #
      # Runs on the dry run too, unlike the cascade gate below: checking the
      # prose is exactly the kind of thing an operator wants to try before
      # committing to a publish.
      #
      # Errors block, nothing softer does. `.vale.ini` sets
      # `MinAlertLevel = suggestion` for authoring; `--minAlertLevel=error`
      # overrides it here so passive voice and long sentences stay out of a
      # release gate. Prose debt must not hold up a fix.
      #
      # Vale is pinned in this repository's .vale-version, read at this
      # workflow's own commit, and the asdf-managed local one names the same
      # version (scripts/vale_version.py), so the same text yields the same
      # alerts in CI and locally.
      - name: Check the release notes with Vale
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || secrets.token }}
          TAG: ${{ steps.draft.outputs.tag }}
          VALE_OUTCOME: ${{ steps.vale.outcome }}
          VALE_RESULT: ${{ steps.vale.outputs.result }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Vale prints the release notes' own text and the consumer's style
          # setup back. Its output passes this filter, which neutralises what the
          # runner reads as a command: a CR (a line end to it) becomes '?', and
          # '##[' becomes '#?[' as in shown() (#492). pipefail keeps Vale's
          # exit status.
          neutralise() { sed -e 's/\r/?/g' -e 's/##\[/#?[/g'; }
          # A download failure warns, it does not block. An unreachable release
          # asset says nothing about the notes, and a release refused for that
          # reason is a worse outcome than one published without a prose check.
          #
          # Every other install failure blocks. A checksum mismatch is not an
          # acquisition failure: an asset replaced under the same tag is exactly
          # the event the pin exists to surface, and the action never ran it.
          # An unknown or missing result blocks too -- fail closed rather than
          # guess that it was harmless.
          if [[ "$VALE_OUTCOME" != "success" ]]; then
            if [[ "$VALE_RESULT" == "download-failed" ]]; then
              echo "::warning::Could not download Vale. Skipping the release-notes check; the notes were NOT verified."
              exit 0
            fi
            echo "::error::Installing Vale failed with result '${VALE_RESULT:-unknown}'. The release-notes check can't run with an unverified binary, and nothing was published. A 'checksum-mismatch' means the release asset no longer matches the SHA-256 pinned in gh-plumbing's .vale-version: investigate before re-running."
            exit 1
          fi

          body=$(gh release view "$TAG" --json body --jq .body)
          if [[ -z "${body//[[:space:]]/}" ]]; then
            echo "::warning::Release notes for '$TAG' are empty; nothing to check."
            exit 0
          fi

          # A style server that can't be reached says nothing about the notes
          # either, so it warns like a download failure. A Vale *finding* is a
          # different matter and does block, below.
          if ! vale sync 2>&1 | neutralise; then
            echo "::warning::'vale sync' could not fetch the style packages. Skipping the release-notes check; the notes were NOT verified."
            exit 0
          fi

          # Written into the repository root so Vale resolves .vale.ini and its
          # `[*.md]` section the same way it does for any documentation page.
          notes=release-notes.vale.md
          trap 'rm -f "$notes"' EXIT
          printf '%s\n' "$body" > "$notes"

          if ! vale --minAlertLevel=error "$notes" 2>&1 | neutralise; then
            echo "::error::The release notes for '$TAG' carry Vale errors. Edit the draft body (gh release edit '$TAG' --notes-file ...) and re-run -- publishing freezes this text."
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "Release notes pass Vale at error level."

      # The pre-release freshness gate the spec asks for (#386 item 3, built in
      # #429). Publishing freezes the documentation alongside the tag: the site
      # deploys from the release, and a page that exists in one language only,
      # or a reference to a workflow that no longer exists, ships with it.
      #
      # Critical findings block, warnings do not -- the same split the checker
      # applies. A parity gap or a dead reference states something false to a
      # reader; an undocumented workflow or a leftover marker is a gap. Holding
      # a release for the second kind would make the gate something to route
      # around. `--strict` at this call site would flip that, deliberately.
      #
      # The checker comes from the pinned checkout ahead of the Vale step.
      - name: Check documentation freshness
        env:
          TAG: ${{ steps.draft.outputs.tag }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The checker's report names the consumer's documentation files.
          # It passes this filter: a CR becomes '?' and '##[' becomes '#?[',
          # as in shown(), so a file name can't start a workflow command
          # (#492). pipefail keeps the checker's exit status.
          neutralise() { sed -e 's/\r/?/g' -e 's/##\[/#?[/g'; }
          # A consumer's checkout never carries this script -- it lives in the
          # repository that ships this workflow, and arrives through the pinned
          # checkout of gh-plumbing. Reading it from the caller would make the
          # gate warn instead of gate for every consumer, which is worse than
          # not having it: a gate that opens when its checker is missing
          # verifies nothing while looking like it does.
          if [[ ! -d docs ]]; then
            echo "::notice::No 'docs/' directory; nothing to audit for freshness."
            exit 0
          fi
          if ! python3 .gh-plumbing/scripts/docs_freshness.py --root . 2>&1 | neutralise; then
            echo "::error::The documentation carries critical freshness findings. Publishing '$TAG' would ship them, because the site and the notes freeze with the tag. Fix them on develop and re-run."
            exit 1
          fi

      # With expected-target-sha set, the target is checked once more right
      # before the flip -- the gates above take minutes, and a branch-named
      # target follows every merge in that window -- and then pinned to the
      # SHA in the same edit that flips the draft, so nothing between this
      # check and the flip can move it (#456).
      # Without the input this step is unchanged.
      - name: Publish (flip draft=false)
        if: ${{ inputs.dry_run != true }}
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || secrets.token }}
          TAG: ${{ steps.draft.outputs.tag }}
          EXPECTED_TARGET_SHA: ${{ inputs.expected-target-sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Masks $1 for a log line (#492): control characters become '?' and
          # '##[' becomes '#?[', so the value can neither end the line nor open
          # the runner's older '##[command]' syntax in the middle of one.
          shown() { local v="${1//[[:cntrl:]]/?}"; printf '%s' "${v//\#\#\[/#?[}"; }
          # Encode, then wrap, for the step summary (#506): a control character
          # becomes a question mark and an ASCII punctuation character its
          # numeric HTML entity (`@` also gets an empty comment after it, so no
          # e-mail autolink forms), inside <code> (md_code) or <pre> (md_pre,
          # line ends kept). Draft, caller and repository text then renders as
          # text and links nothing.
          md_enc() { local LC_ALL=C; local s="${1//[[:cntrl:]]/?}" c n x; s="${s//$'\xc2'[$'\x80'-$'\x9f']/?}"; s="${s//$'\xe2\x80'[$'\xa8\xa9']/?}"; for n in {33..47} {58..64} {91..96} {123..126}; do printf -v x '%x' "$n"; printf -v c '%b' "\\x$x"; s=${s//"$c"/$'\x01'$n$'\x02'}; done; s=${s//$'\x01'64$'\x02'/$'\x01'64$'\x02\x03'}; s=${s//$'\x01'/'&#'}; s=${s//$'\x02'/';'}; s=${s//$'\x03'/'<!-- -->'}; printf '%s' "$s"; }
          md_code() { printf '<code>%s</code>' "$(md_enc "$1")"; }
          md_pre() { local line; printf '<pre>'; while IFS= read -r line; do md_enc "${line%$'\r'}"; printf '\n'; done <<< "$1"; printf '</pre>\n'; }
          if [[ -n "$EXPECTED_TARGET_SHA" ]]; then
            expected="${EXPECTED_TARGET_SHA,,}"
            # Same resolution as the Resolve draft step above.
            resolve_commit() {
              local ref="$1"
              if [[ "$ref" =~ ^[0-9a-fA-F]{40}$ ]]; then
                echo "${ref,,}"
              elif git rev-parse --verify --quiet "origin/${ref#refs/heads/}^{commit}"; then
                :
              else
                git rev-parse --verify --quiet "${ref}^{commit}"
              fi
            }

            git fetch --quiet origin
            target=$(gh release view "$TAG" --json targetCommitish --jq .targetCommitish)
            # Masked for printing only, as in Resolve draft.
            shown_target=$(shown "$target")
            if ! actual=$(resolve_commit "$target"); then
              echo "::error::Draft '$TAG' target '$shown_target' resolves to no commit on origin; not publishing."
              exit 1
            fi
            if [[ "$actual" != "$expected" ]]; then
              echo "::error::Draft '$TAG' now targets $actual (from '$shown_target'), but the archive was built from $expected. The target moved while this run was checking it -- a merge on the target branch or an edited draft. Nothing was published; rebuild the archive from the current draft target, then publish again."
              exit 1
            fi
            # One edit pins the target and flips the draft, so no second call
            # leaves a window in which the target could change again.
            gh release edit "$TAG" --target "$expected" --draft=false
            echo "Pinned draft '$TAG' target to $expected and flipped it."
          else
            gh release edit "$TAG" --draft=false
          fi
          published_at=$(date -Is)
          echo "Published $TAG at $published_at."
          echo "::notice::Published $TAG at $published_at."
          {
            echo
            echo "### Published"
            echo
            echo "- $(md_code "$TAG") flipped to \`draft: false\` at $(md_code "$published_at")."
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      - name: Dry-run summary
        if: ${{ inputs.dry_run == true }}
        env:
          TAG: ${{ steps.draft.outputs.tag }}
        run: |
          # Encode, then wrap, for the step summary (#506): a control character
          # becomes a question mark and an ASCII punctuation character its
          # numeric HTML entity (`@` also gets an empty comment after it, so no
          # e-mail autolink forms), inside <code> (md_code) or <pre> (md_pre,
          # line ends kept). Draft, caller and repository text then renders as
          # text and links nothing.
          md_enc() { local LC_ALL=C; local s="${1//[[:cntrl:]]/?}" c n x; s="${s//$'\xc2'[$'\x80'-$'\x9f']/?}"; s="${s//$'\xe2\x80'[$'\xa8\xa9']/?}"; for n in {33..47} {58..64} {91..96} {123..126}; do printf -v x '%x' "$n"; printf -v c '%b' "\\x$x"; s=${s//"$c"/$'\x01'$n$'\x02'}; done; s=${s//$'\x01'64$'\x02'/$'\x01'64$'\x02\x03'}; s=${s//$'\x01'/'&#'}; s=${s//$'\x02'/';'}; s=${s//$'\x03'/'<!-- -->'}; printf '%s' "$s"; }
          md_code() { printf '<code>%s</code>' "$(md_enc "$1")"; }
          md_pre() { local line; printf '<pre>'; while IFS= read -r line; do md_enc "${line%$'\r'}"; printf '\n'; done <<< "$1"; printf '</pre>\n'; }
          {
            echo
            echo "### Dry run"
            echo
            echo "- All gates passed for $(md_code "$TAG")."
            echo "- \`gh release edit --draft=false\` was **not** called."
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      # Pitfall 1: re-read isDraft after the flip and fail loudly if the release
      # is still a draft. `gh release edit --draft=false` (and any automerge-style
      # wrapper around it) can exit 0 without the draft actually flipping — the
      # silent-success footgun #375 names. Never trust the publish step's exit
      # code alone; verify the observable state.
      - name: Post-publish sanity
        if: ${{ inputs.dry_run != true }}
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || secrets.token }}
          TAG: ${{ steps.draft.outputs.tag }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          is_draft=$(gh release view "$TAG" --json isDraft --jq .isDraft)
          if [[ "$is_draft" != "false" ]]; then
            echo "::error::Post-publish check failed: '$TAG' still reports isDraft=$is_draft after the flip (expected false). The publish step exited 0 but the draft did not flip — re-run release-publish or flip the draft manually (gh release edit '$TAG' --draft=false)."
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "Post-publish: isDraft=false confirmed."

      # Pitfall 2: deterministic cascade-gap warning bound to the fallback
      # condition itself. steps.app-token.outputs.token is empty in exactly the
      # two cases the issue names — inputs.app-id unset (mint step skipped) or
      # the App-token mint failed (continue-on-error) — so this fires precisely
      # when the release:published event was authored by GITHUB_TOKEN and will
      # NOT cascade. Surfaced in the job summary, not just the log.
      - name: Warn on GITHUB_TOKEN cascade gap
        if: ${{ inputs.dry_run != true && steps.app-token.outputs.token == '' }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          msg="Published under GITHUB_TOKEN (no portfolio App token: inputs.app-id unset or the App-token mint failed). The release:published event will NOT cascade to release-cd-refresh-master.yml / release-cd-deliver-docs.yml — main and the docs will not refresh automatically. Dispatch release-cd-refresh-master.yml manually to fast-forward main (spec/project/workflow-health/ §Known platform constraints, #330)."
          echo "::warning::$msg"
          {
            echo
            echo "### ⚠️ Cascade gap (GITHUB_TOKEN fallback)"
            echo
            echo "$msg"
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      # Belt-and-suspenders runtime probe — only when an App token WAS used and
      # the cascade is therefore expected to fire. Gating on token != '' keeps
      # this neutral/informational note from contradicting the deterministic
      # cascade-gap warning above (the two conditions are mutually exclusive).
      - name: Probe cascade run (App token path)
        if: ${{ inputs.dry_run != true && steps.app-token.outputs.token != '' }}
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || secrets.token }}
          TARGET_SHA: ${{ steps.align.outputs.target_sha || steps.draft.outputs.target_sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Masks $1 for a log line (#492): control characters become '?' and
          # '##[' becomes '#?[', so the value can neither end the line nor open
          # the runner's older '##[command]' syntax in the middle of one.
          shown() { local v="${1//[[:cntrl:]]/?}"; printf '%s' "${v//\#\#\[/#?[}"; }
          # The cascade run may not have registered yet; this is a best-effort
          # probe, never an error (spec/project/workflow-health/ §Known platform constraints).
          sleep 30
          refresh_run=$(gh run list --workflow=release-cd-refresh-master.yml --limit 1 --json status,createdAt,headSha --jq '.[0]')
          if [[ -z "$refresh_run" || "$refresh_run" == "null" ]]; then
            echo "::notice::No recent release-cd-refresh-master.yml run observed yet for $TARGET_SHA. The App-authored release:published event should cascade shortly; if main does not refresh, dispatch release-cd-refresh-master.yml manually."
          else
            # An API response, one line of JSON; masked like the others (#492).
            echo "release-cd-refresh-master.yml run detected: $(shown "$refresh_run")"
          fi

name: Release Deliver to Master

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      from_branch:
        description: |
          Git ref the presentation branch is reset to -- normally the published
          release tag. Defaults to `github.event.release.tag_name`, which the
          `release` payload actually carries. It previously defaulted to
          `github.event.ref`, a field that payload does NOT carry: the value
          resolved to the empty string on every release, and the old merge step
          silently fell back to the default branch. The presentation branch
          therefore tracked `develop`'s tip rather than the release tag, and
          only looked right because tags are cut at that tip.
        required: false
        default: ${{ github.event.release.tag_name }}
        type: string
      target_branch:
        required: false
        default: master
        type: string
      app-id:
        description: |
          Numeric GitHub App ID of the portfolio App. When set, the
          reusable mints a short-lived installation token from
          `secrets.app-private-key` and uses it for the master fast-
          forward. When empty (the default), the reusable falls
          through to `secrets.token` — typically the consumer's
          `GITHUB_TOKEN`. Where the target branch carries a push
          restriction (`restrictions.apps: [<app-slug>]`, available on
          organisation-owned repositories only), `GITHUB_TOKEN` has no
          right to push to it and the App token is mandatory.
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ""
    secrets:
      token:
        required: true
      app-private-key:
        description: |
          PEM-encoded private key for the App identified by `inputs.app-id`.
          Required when `app-id` is set; ignored otherwise.
        required: false
# Explicit permissions per spec/project/github-actions-best-practices §B:
# workflow level is the minimum, write scopes are granted per job.
permissions:
  contents: read


# Every run of this workflow updates the same presentation branch, so two
# releases published close together race on one target. The group is static
# rather than ref-derived on purpose: the contended resource is the target
# branch, not the ref that triggered the run, and two runs from different tags
# still collide. Matches the `release-publish` group in
# reusable-release-publish.yml.
#
# cancel-in-progress stays false per spec/project/github-actions-best-practices
# §F: a delivery workflow must never cancel an in-flight run.
concurrency:
  group: release-cd-refresh-master
  cancel-in-progress: false


jobs:
  refresh_presentation_branch:
    permissions:
      contents: write # fast-forwards the presentation branch
    name: "Publish the the Release to Master"
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      # Mint an App installation token only when the caller has set
      # inputs.app-id. The output token replaces secrets.token for the
      # checkout and the push via the
      # `steps.app-token.outputs.token || secrets.token` fallback.
      - name: Mint App installation token
        id: app-token
        if: ${{ inputs.app-id != '' }}
        # Tolerate a half-configured setup. On any failure outputs.token
        # is empty and the fallback to secrets.token kicks in — note
        # that on a protected master with `restrictions.apps`, the
        # fallback will fail at push time; the operator must complete
        # Phase 0 (variable + secret) before this workflow can
        # succeed on a fully-restricted master.
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/create-github-app-token@fee1f7d63c2ff003460e3d139729b119787bc349 # v2.2.2
        with:
          app-id: ${{ inputs.app-id }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.app-private-key }}

      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@d23441a48e516b6c34aea4fa41551a30e30af803 # v6.1.0
        with:
          # Full history plus tags: the reset resolves an arbitrary ref to a
          # commit, which a shallow clone cannot do.
          fetch-depth: 0
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || secrets.token }}
          # Kept: the "Refresh the presentation branch" step runs
          # `git fetch`, `git ls-remote` and `git push` against origin.
          persist-credentials: true

      # A single write strategy cannot serve every presentation branch, because
      # real consumer configurations forbid opposite things (issue #414):
      #
      #   linear history  -> no merge commits  -> the merge is rejected
      #   no force pushes -> no rewrite        -> the reset is rejected
      #
      # ADR-001 chose the reset to solve the first and did not consider the
      # second. `gh-plumbing`'s own master is the second case, which is why
      # v2.0.0 and v2.0.1 both published green while master stayed on v1.1.26.
      #
      # So the strategy is read from the target rather than assumed. Both
      # mechanisms have to be consulted -- classic protection and rulesets are
      # independent, and either can forbid either operation.
      - name: Determine the write strategy from the target's protection
        id: strategy
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || secrets.token }}
          TARGET: ${{ inputs.target_branch }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Masks $1 for a log line (#492): control characters become '?' and
          # '##[' becomes '#?[', so the value can neither end the line nor open
          # the runner's older '##[command]' syntax in the middle of one.
          shown() { local v="${1//[[:cntrl:]]/?}"; printf '%s' "${v//\#\#\[/#?[}"; }

          # An unreadable endpoint must not read as "unrestricted": that is the
          # mistake the branch-protection audit made (#421). Unknown means the
          # restriction is assumed to be present, so the run degrades to a
          # refusal with a diagnosis rather than a rejected push.
          classic=$(gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/branches/${TARGET}/protection" 2>/dev/null || echo '')
          rules=$(gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/rules/branches/${TARGET}" 2>/dev/null || echo '[]')

          rule_types=$(echo "$rules" | jq -r '[.[]?.type] | unique | join(",")')

          # `pull_request` blocks every direct write, merge and reset alike.
          blocks_direct=$(echo "$rules" | jq -r 'any(.[]?; .type == "pull_request")')
          # Force push: classic `allow_force_pushes`, and the `non_fast_forward`
          # rule which forbids any history rewrite.
          rule_no_force=$(echo "$rules" | jq -r 'any(.[]?; .type == "non_fast_forward")')
          classic_force=$(echo "${classic:-{\}}" | jq -r '.allow_force_pushes.enabled // false')
          # Merge commits: classic and ruleset linear-history both forbid them.
          rule_linear=$(echo "$rules" | jq -r 'any(.[]?; .type == "required_linear_history")')
          classic_linear=$(echo "${classic:-{\}}" | jq -r '.required_linear_history.enabled // false')

          force_ok=false
          [ "$classic_force" = "true" ] && [ "$rule_no_force" != "true" ] && force_ok=true
          merge_ok=false
          [ "$classic_linear" != "true" ] && [ "$rule_linear" != "true" ] && merge_ok=true

          if [ "$blocks_direct" = "true" ]; then
            mode=blocked
            reason="a \`pull_request\` ruleset rule requires every change to arrive through a pull request, so neither a merge nor a reset may be pushed directly"
          elif [ "$merge_ok" = "true" ]; then
            # Preferred over the reset when both are available: it adds to the
            # branch instead of rewriting it, so a consumer holding anything on
            # the presentation branch does not lose it.
            mode=merge
            reason="merge commits are permitted"
          elif [ "$force_ok" = "true" ]; then
            mode=reset
            reason="merge commits are forbidden, force pushes are permitted"
          else
            mode=blocked
            reason="the target forbids merge commits and force pushes alike"
          fi

          {
            echo "mode=$mode"
            echo "reason=$reason"
          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          # target_branch and from_branch are caller input. This job's own log
          # messages print them through shown() (#492), the step summaries
          # below through md_code() (#506); git's own output prints them as
          # they are.
          echo "Strategy for '$(shown "$TARGET")': ${mode} -- ${reason}"
          echo "  classic protection readable: $([ -n "$classic" ] && echo yes || echo 'no (absent or unreadable)')"
          echo "  ruleset rules: ${rule_types:-(none)}"

      - name: Refresh the presentation branch
        id: refresh
        if: steps.strategy.outputs.mode != 'blocked'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || secrets.token }}
          FROM_REF: ${{ inputs.from_branch }}
          TARGET: ${{ inputs.target_branch }}
          MODE: ${{ steps.strategy.outputs.mode }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Masks $1 for a log line (#492): control characters become '?' and
